newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PM says '96 budget shows CZK 418 mln surplus.
newsitem.headline: Czech PM says '96 budget shows CZK 418 mln surplus.

text.p: Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus said on Thursday that he was "very happy" that the state budget was in surplus for the fourth consecutive year in 1996 and had not recorded a deficit as expected earlier.

Klaus's office reported in a statement that results showed the 1996 budget ended with a 418 million crown surplus. Earlier the finance ministry told the local agency CTK that preliminary data showed a 419 million crown surplus.
"(The prime minister) is very happy that the current numbers show a surplus in the budget in the amount of 418 million crowns," said the statement issued by Klaus's spokesman Ivo Strejcek.
"The prime minister expressed his satisfaction that through all the complexities of 1996, that it was still possible the keep the state budget for the year in balance."

The government froze selective spending in December, and combined with early payments on credit due from non-budget government agencies, forecast a deficit of 1.2 billion crowns, instead of the more than five billion crown shortfall it feared.

In the autumn the government made across-the-board spending cuts to avoid a forecast 9.3 billion crown shortfall, caused by high-than-expected spending, slow repayments on credits to Russia, and lower-than-expected tax revenue.
The 1996 budget was originally approved as a balanced budget totalling 497 billion crowns, but the autumn spending cuts knocked the forecast expenditure down to 491 billion crowns.
Klaus governments have managed four straight budgets ending with a surplus, and parliament approved a fifth straight balanced budget plan in December.
